## Source: amazon-inspector (6dc8c3628b1d44eca51a5cde6143c1760a5d393b45729f174bab73f76f8641e8)
Package publishes under the `@securihackbot` scope as a public dependency-confusion squat of an internal name. The declared `postinstall` script executes `postinstall.js`, which on `npm install` collects host identifiers (os.hostname(), USER/USERNAME, platform, arch, node version, package name, and a nonce), base64-encodes them, and sends them as a query parameter via plain-HTTP GET to a hardcoded bare-IP collector at http://34.143.131.27:18080/. A DNS-exfil fallback resolves NONCE-prefixed subdomains under a configured DNS suffix. The exfiltration fires automatically on install with no opt-in, and any build host whose resolver pulls this public tarball instead of an intended internal `@securihackbot/*` package will beacon host metadata to the hardcoded collector. The 'authorized research' framing in the README does not gate the behavior, which runs against any installer that resolves this version.
